rationale: The frozen kernel contract is BEHAVIOR ONLY: the CLI verbs/flags, the awa-worktree/v1 dashboard JSON shape, the guard permission schema, the .awa/lease.json shape, and (added additive-within-v1 2026-07-08) the clean_receipt/v1 receipt shape and the active_root/v1 heartbeat shape. The 2026-07-10 Root-Bound Worktree Finish extensions are additive-within-v1: Phase 1 added optional clean flags, receipt fields, session membership, and awa_finish_challenge/v1; Phase 2 adds optional finish intent/dialogue/warning/protected-Retain/hook surfaces that only route to Phase 1 and add no removal authority. No existing verb/flag/key/schema-string changed; every existing v1 consumer stays valid; NO v2. These surfaces are the kernel's public interface; the engine may only BACK them, never silently change them. Removing/renaming a required verb/flag/key, or changing a schema string, is a breaking change that requires a versioned bump (awa-contract.v2.json). Additive, backward-compatible fields (new OPTIONAL keys) are allowed WITHIN v1. FILE LOCATIONS ARE NOT FROZEN: the shim/hook/emitter paths recorded below are informational and resolved by ROLE (AWA_HOME / the installed release path / a host overlay), because location was never the interface. Re-homing the generic kernel from a host's _ops/ into KleinPerkins/awa/kernel/ therefore needs NO contract bump (D-CONTRACT). The in-repo role-resolved freeze checker (kernel/checks/awa-contract-freeze.sh) enforces the behavior floor against the live shims wherever they are installed.

informational.note: NOT part of the frozen interface. These record where the reference implementation ships inside KleinPerkins/awa; hosts/installs MAY relocate them. The freeze checker resolves the live shims BY ROLE (AWA_HOME or the installed path), never by these literals.

hook_ownership.direct_rule: AWA reconciles exactly the five declared logical roles in the selected Cursor user hook file while preserving unrelated rows.
hook_ownership.external_rule: The external host owns the complete selected hook file. AWA installs and validates its product runtime but does not read, stat, create, back up, chmod, rewrite, or remove that hook file on install, repair, doctor, or uninstall.
hook_ownership.role_identity_rule: A logical role is identified by its stable id plus event, never by command-path spelling. Direct and external path projections of one role must not coexist in a converged host matrix.
hook_ownership.host_policy_delegator_rule: A host-policy-delegator may inject only host policy/root data and then execute the matching installed AWA role. Missing or failed delegation remains fail-open and may not fork guard or session semantics.

cli.tool_note: INFORMATIONAL — reference-impl location, NOT frozen. Resolved by role (AWA_HOME/kernel/bin/dev-worktree.sh or the installed release). Only the verbs + flags below are frozen behavior.
cli.clean_finish_flags_note: ADDITIVE-WITHIN-v1 (2026-07-10 Phase 1; 2026-07-11 hook-generation binding; 2026-07-15 semantic drift binding). --finish-current discards + removes the CURRENT linked worktree (takes NO --path; the target is the physical current dir, which must equal `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` AND be a linked worktree — git-dir != git-common-dir — never the primary checkout). --preview is READ-ONLY (render the at-risk inventory + create a pending challenge; no fetch/push/branch/archive/mutation). The --finish-current flag is NOT authorization: removal requires --authorization to be EXACTLY `Close` and, under the per-common-dir lock, either the challenge's full fingerprint to byte-equal or its path-granularity structural fingerprint to byte-equal. The structural proof exact-binds ordered displayed deletion scopes, each row-root type/mode/link target, directory and symlink descendants, all physical structure outside displayed directory scopes, Git path/mode/stage structure, operation state, target identity, and session membership. Regular files below an already displayed directory scope are its opaque contents, so their creation/removal/rename/mode/bytes and ordinary index blob ids are omitted; changing the displayed scope, any directory/symlink descendant, or any structure outside it refuses. A legacy challenge without this additive proof remains full-fingerprint-only. --conversation-id keys the pending challenge. Hook mode additionally requires paired --expected-nonce/--expected-generation exact-binding fields from the consumed envelope/dialogue and claims that generation before the lock attempt; direct non-hook Phase-1 preview/Close remains compatible without them. The finish path uses the finish-only per-session gate (NOT the frozen --path active-root gate); ordinary `clean --path` KEEPS its v1 active-root + --force semantics UNCHANGED and does NOT reuse the finish authorization.

dashboard_data.additive_note: The Phase-0/8 dashboard (X4) MAY add OPTIONAL top-level/summary keys (e.g. promise-state, scope, degraded, stale) additively without a version bump; the required key sets above are the immutable floor. Per-repo MODE is ON/OFF and ADDITIVE WITHIN v1 — NOT a v2: the OPTIONAL keys repo.mode (on|off|invalid|"") and repo.mode_error MAY be emitted without a version bump. The required summary_keys/repo_keys floors and the guard permission_values ([allow, ask, deny]) are UNCHANGED; existing awa-worktree/v1 consumers stay valid. Historical breadcrumb: an interim ASK_ON mode + an OPTIONAL summary.ask_on key were REMOVED 2026-07-07 when primary-checkout protection moved from unenforced `ask` to enforced `deny`; classify() now emits only include|exclude|advisory|not-git, and only `off` disables (any other value resolves to on/include).

guard_permission.hook_note: INFORMATIONAL — reference-impl location, NOT frozen. Resolved by role (AWA_HOME/kernel/hooks/worktree-guard.sh or the installed release). Only the permission schema below is frozen behavior.
guard_permission.note: beforeShellExecution is the pre-mutation gate. Cursor ENFORCES `deny` but treats `ask` as NON-BLOCKING on the agent path (L4), so a CONFIRMED mutating command on an INCLUDED PRIMARY checkout (mode ON) returns `deny` (deny_shape); `ask` remains in the vocabulary as an honest no-op on the genuine-uncertainty path (an included-looking checkout with an unparseable payload). afterFileEdit is observation-only: the guard MUST return allow there and MUST NOT emit a no-op ask (X2). A Cursor Cloud / background agent degrades to allow BEFORE the deny branch (an already-isolated /workspace clone is never hard-blocked).

lease.identity_rule: lease_id = hash(worktree_path + branch + git_common_dir + boot_id). NEVER a bare pid (a pid is reused across reboots/processes). pid MAY be recorded as an informational field but is never the identity.
lease.collision_boundary: The per-git_common_dir advisory lock (git rev-parse --git-common-dir) is the real collision boundary; branch/path uniqueness is necessary but not sufficient.
lease.wal_placement: SQLite state.db and its -wal/-shm sidecars MUST live under ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/awa on local disk, never a cloud-synced/network path.
lease.note: No component emits a lease yet (recovery/engine unbuilt). This shape is the FORWARD contract the kernel/engine must back when leases land (Phase 2). awa-contract-freeze.sh validates any lease file that DOES exist against this shape.

clean_receipt.emitted_by_role: EVERY terminal `clean` path — kernel dev-worktree.sh `clean` (incl. --bundle / --force / --delete-branch) AND every refusal/error return. Kernel-owned, holds engine-OFF and router-OFF.

finish_fields.note: ADDITIVE-WITHIN-v1 (2026-07-10) OPTIONAL top-level fields populated ONLY on the `clean --finish-current` path; on the ordinary `clean --path` path they carry their defaults so every existing clean_receipt/v1 consumer stays valid.
finish_fields.branch_action_rule: The branch decision is network-free (LOCAL refs only — no gh/fetch/ls-remote). retained_local_only = the branch has commits not reachable from any other local/remote-tracking ref (kept). deleted = an AWA-attested ephemeral branch with an EMPTY local-only set, compare-and-deleted at the captured HEAD AFTER worktree removal, with the actual files/reftable namespaces physically synced. delete_failed = compare-and-delete did not occur and the branch remains. delete_error = a classified post-removal branch command failure with the branch retained. A logical deletion whose backend durability cannot be certified has no branch_action and produces workspace_removed:null until journal reconciliation re-syncs and records exact truth. retained = kept for any other non-delete disposition.
finish_fields.finish_authorization_rule: Removal happens ONLY when, under the shared per-common-dir lock, a freshly recomputed full content fingerprint OR path-granularity structural fingerprint byte-equals the pending challenge AND the answer is EXACTLY the literal `Close` (case-sensitive, standalone). The full private proof includes encoded raw relative path, type, mode bits, size, regular-file SHA-256, symlink target, exact Git status/index evidence, and every sorted descendant of grouped directories for every filesystem object in the worktree. The structural proof exact-binds displayed deletion scopes and non-content structure while treating regular files below an already displayed directory as opaque contents of that authorized scope. Files are opened no-follow and lstat/open/fstat/re-lstat identity must remain stable; any read/structural drift/special-file/mount/escape/deep nested-repository uncertainty PRESERVES the worktree. Operator/hook diagnostics expose only stable escaped rows, never private descendant paths, content, hashes, or link-target proof. finish_preview is a READ-ONLY terminal path (disposition refused: nothing removed) that renders the inventory and creates the pending challenge.
finish_fields.finish_index_visibility_rule: Before every finish status/filesystem inventory and before challenge creation, the kernel runs a read-only, NUL-safe index-visibility preflight. Any assume-unchanged entry, skip-worktree/sparse entry or active sparse-checkout configuration, fsmonitor-valid extension/entry or effective fsmonitor configuration, malformed/ambiguous output, unsupported split visibility, or inspection failure refuses with the single content-safe reason `index_visibility_flags`; unchanged flagged entries refuse too. The probe supports SHA-1 and SHA-256 indexes, passes `core.fsmonitor=false`, sets `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` and `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, never invokes fsmonitor/clean/smudge filters, and never exposes paths, object ids, hashes, config values, stderr, or contents. Refusal creates no challenge/dialogue and preserves the root. This is finish-only: ordinary `clean --path` v1 behavior is unchanged.
finish_fields.finish_no_network_rule: The finish removal path and its branch decision perform ZERO network calls (no gh / git fetch / git ls-remote). Delivery verification is deferred (Phase 2 Commit).

clean_receipt.every_terminal_path_rule: A receipt is written on EVERY terminal clean path — success, every refusal, and error (guaranteed by an EXIT trap with a fail-safe refusal default). A new terminal clean path that emits no receipt is a contract violation (parametrized test fails CI). A disposition outside disposition_values is coerced to `refused` — a mis-wired path can never mint a spurious `removed`.
clean_receipt.bundle_rule: `clean --bundle` STAYS contract-compatible WITHIN v1 (the v7 resolution, not reopened): --bundle remains a frozen `clean` flag and the terminal path is honored (archive-then-remove) with flags.bundle=true recorded. It is NOT a new verb and needs NO v2.
clean_receipt.ignored_files_are_child_state: Ignored files count as CHILD STATE (not safe-to-delete): a clean with ignored files present REFUSES (reason_code contains `ignored`) unless --bundle (archive first) or --force (explicit override).
clean_receipt.unknown_evidence_blocks: If child-state evidence cannot be gathered (e.g. the ignored-file scan itself fails), the terminal path REFUSES (reason_code ignored_scan_failed) rather than proceeding — unknown/unattributed evidence blocks a destructive action.
clean_receipt.clean_lock_rule: ADDITIVE-WITHIN-v1 (2026-07-10). The ORDINARY `clean --path` destructive section (the TOCTOU disposition re-read + `git worktree remove` + branch-delete) is held under the SAME per-common-dir advisory lock ABI as kernel finish + engine maintenance (LOCK_EX on locks/common-<key>.lock, key = sha256(abspath(common_dir))[:24]), so an ordinary clean serializes against a concurrent finish/engine mutation on the same git_common_dir. Uncontended acquisition is transparent (no behavior change). On contention within the bounded acquire timeout the clean REFUSES fail-safe (disposition refused, reason_code clean_lock_busy) and PRESERVES the worktree. This does NOT lock a worktree against removal (disposition remains advisory kernel state) — it is write-serialization only.
clean_receipt.fail_closed_rule: The active-root gate fails CLOSED on UNCERTAINTY, never open: if the canonical-disposition tool is unavailable (empty/non-zero output) the clean REFUSES (reason_code disposition_unavailable); if the kernel lib itself is missing the clean REFUSES (reason_code roots_lib_missing); a root re-activated mid-clean REFUSES (reason_code reactivated_during_clean). An operator `--force` (explicit ack) may override an unavailable/lib-missing/fail-safe-active gate — never a genuine live-session active.
clean_receipt.receipt_write_failure_rule: A receipt-write failure is NOT swallowed: the kernel emits a stderr breadcrumb and, on an otherwise-successful clean, surfaces a non-zero AUDIT status (exit 3) so a removal with no durable record is never reported as a clean success.
clean_receipt.storage: clean-<receipt_id>.json under ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/awa/receipts (dir 700, file 600), local disk. NEVER read from any router artifact.
clean_receipt.k2_todo: DEFERRED (K2 observability, not a safety gap): receipts/ grows unbounded — add a prune/TTL + size cap. The safety-relevant record escape (`forget` / --force) already ships.
clean_receipt.note: Additive-within v1 (a new OPTIONAL top-level schema block, 2026-07-08; fail-closed hardening + audit-status fields added 2026-07-08; OPTIONAL finish_fields added 2026-07-10 for Root-Bound Worktree Finish Phase 1). Existing awa-contract v1 consumers stay valid; NO v2.

awa_finish_challenge.emitted_by_role: kernel/lib/awa_finish.py (driven by `dev-worktree.sh clean --finish-current --preview`). Kernel-owned, stdlib-only; holds engine-OFF and router-OFF.
awa_finish_challenge.purpose: A CONTENT-ADDRESSED pending authorization for a root-bound worktree finish. The challenge binds the exact target (canonical root/git_dir/common_dir, branch, HEAD, install identity, and root/Git-admin physical incarnations), a full SHA-256 fingerprint of all at-risk bytes, an additive structural SHA-256 fingerprint of the ordered displayed deletion scopes and physical structure, operation markers, other-session heartbeat membership, physical incarnations, classification versions, and a random nonce. Removal is authorized ONLY when, under the per-common-dir lock, the full fingerprint OR the path-granularity structural fingerprint byte-equals this challenge AND the operator answer is the exact literal `Close`. Structural equality may tolerate regular-file creation/removal/rename/mode/byte changes below an already displayed directory scope because the warning authorizes that complete scope. Every displayed-row insertion/removal/reorder/path/root-type/root-mode/root-link change, directory or symlink descendant change, structure change outside such a scope, Git path/mode/stage change, operation-state change, target change, or membership change refuses.
awa_finish_challenge.content_addressed_rule: Authorization is content-addressed, NOT time-boxed: full-fingerprint or structural-fingerprint byte-equality (re-derived under the lock) is the mechanism. The structural fingerprint preserves displayed row order and normalized deletion-scope paths, binds each row-root type/mode/link target, every directory/symlink descendant, physical structure outside displayed directory scopes, exact Git index path/mode/stage structure, operation state, target identity, and session membership. It treats regular files below an already displayed directory scope as opaque row content and omits their presence/name/mode/bytes plus ordinary index blob ids. The additive operation_digest remains full-content and exact-binds the canonical private Git-operation manifest (including raw index, logical refs, object closure, admin topology/content, and required worktree dependencies). Legacy challenges without structure_fingerprint remain full-fingerprint-only. There is NO separate short-lived execution-permit window to race.
awa_finish_challenge.staleness_backstop: A SINGLE coarse staleness backstop (default 900s; env AWA_FINISH_CHALLENGE_TTL_SECONDS, floored at 60s) discards an ABANDONED challenge. This is a BACKSTOP for cleanup, never the authorization mechanism.
awa_finish_challenge.replay_once_rule: For hook mode, each activated Close nonce+generation is atomically claimed in awa_finish_generation_state/v1 BEFORE the shared-lock attempt or any destructive action. That generation is permanently inert after the first kernel execution attempt, including binding/session/fingerprint/final-recheck/removal/cleanup failure and lock contention; retry requires a fresh preview and fresh envelope. Direct non-hook Phase-1 compatibility remains challenge-based. The confirming session's own heartbeat timestamp is deliberately NOT stored in the challenge.
awa_finish_challenge.no_network_rule: Creating, reading, consuming, and acting on a challenge perform ZERO network calls.
awa_finish_challenge.storage: challenge-<conversation_key>.json under ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/awa/finish (dir 700, file 600), local disk. This challenge file is a projection, not terminal-generation authority. NEVER read from any router artifact.
awa_finish_challenge.note: NEW OPTIONAL top-level block, additive-within v1 (2026-07-10, Root-Bound Worktree Finish Phase 1). No existing v1 consumer is affected; NO v2.

awa_git_operation_manifest.private_rule: Under the one shared per-common-dir lock, the kernel captures every supported per-worktree Git operation as one canonical private content-addressed manifest. It recursively scans only regular files/directories descriptor-relative and no-follow, sorted by raw-byte relative name, and binds type/mode/size/SHA-256, exact raw index bytes plus parsed stages, logical refs read through Git's ref API (including refs/bisect and refs/rewritten for files or reftable), operation-reachable object closure, original/head identity, and all index/worktree dependencies. It scans the operation state twice around complete worktree capture and requires byte equality. Links, special files, mount crossings, live git lockfiles (a genuine top-level git lock -- a git-managed lockable stem or a `<f>.lock` over an existing top-level `<f>`; a foreign non-git `.lock` such as the host `cursor-session.lock` session marker is ignored, never a live lock), path escapes, unknown/ambiguous combinations, malformed refs/indexes, missing objects, and read drift refuse safely.
awa_git_operation_manifest.row_rule: Each logical active group adds exactly one fixed content-safe synthetic warning row. It contains no object id, message, todo, patch, or admin path; commit_eligible=false, retain_eligible=true. It participates in fingerprint, discard count, and receipt. Exact Close may discard it only through the unchanged warning/challenge/authorization protocol.
awa_git_operation_manifest.detached_rule: A detached worktree is previewable only when the canonical active operation names exactly one live original refs/heads branch. That branch is the effective identity and is always retained as a recovery anchor. Detached HEAD without a recognized complete operation remains refused.
awa_git_operation_manifest.note: NEW OPTIONAL top-level block, additive-within v1 (2026-07-11 Critical operation-state certification hardening).

awa_kernel_durability.implementation_role: kernel/lib/awa_durability.py, shared by awa_finish.py and awa_roots.py
awa_kernel_durability.rule: Critical kernel state uses one stdlib primitive for complete EINTR-safe writes, atomic private replace, exclusive create, durable unlink/adoption, and private directory creation one component at a time. _sync_fd always retries fsync on EINTR; Linux uses fsync, while Darwin additionally requires successful F_FULLFSYNC for regular files and directories with absence/failure propagated and no downgrade. This applies to install identity, challenge migration/create/publication/activation, generation claim/cancel, active/current sessions, prepared/removed/finalized removal journals, durable branch outcome, receipts, CAS unlinks, and critical namespace creation. Lock PID text and never-promoted scratch are noncritical.
awa_kernel_durability.ordering_rule: Failures before Git removal preserve the root. Failures after logical removal report workspace_removed:null until namespace and branch truth are physically certified. Receipt failure leaves retryable removed state; cleanup failures after certified removal are bounded warnings.
awa_kernel_durability.note: NEW OPTIONAL top-level block, additive-within v1 (2026-07-11 Critical physical-durability certification hardening).

awa_finish_generation_state.one_use_rule: A nonce+generation-bound 0600 record is created with exclusive-create semantics. close_claimed is written before the shared-lock attempt and makes an activated hook Close generation permanently unreadable as live authority. Any existing terminal record, including malformed or conflicting state, fails closed and cannot be overwritten.
awa_finish_generation_state.generation_binding_rule: If either expected field is supplied, hook-mode execution requires a complete valid nonce+generation pair supplied from the consumed choice envelope/dialogue, requires the current challenge itself to remain hook-mode, and exact-matches both fields before claim. A replacement-generation race—including replacement by a direct challenge—refuses without consuming the replacement. Direct non-hook Phase-1 execution remains compatible only when both expected fields are absent.
awa_finish_generation_state.cancel_rule: Cancel first writes the cancelled terminal transition, making that exact generation inert before bounded challenge/dialogue/current-index/choice-envelope projection cleanup. Readers reject terminal generations even if cleanup fails. Incomplete cleanup is reported as failure with explicit state-cleanup warnings; Cancel never mutates repository, archive, git, worktree, or network state.
awa_finish_generation_state.storage: generation-<conversation_key>-<generation>-<nonce_digest>.json under ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/awa/finish (dir 700, file 600), local disk. Terminal records are retained as replay/audit authority.
awa_finish_generation_state.note: NEW OPTIONAL top-level block, additive-within v1 (2026-07-11, Root-Bound Worktree Finish Phase 2 hardening). No existing v1 consumer is affected; NO v2.

awa_finish_removal.transaction_rule: Before Git removal, the kernel atomically writes and physically syncs a 0600 operation-identity-bound prepared journal and its parent directory under the same per-common-dir lock. The journal retains the warning-time fingerprint and separately binds the execution_fingerprint observed in the final under-lock inventory; present-root recovery must byte-match execution_fingerprint before clearing a failed pre-removal attempt. Reconciliation requires both exact physical-root existence and local `git worktree list --porcelain -z` registration; one signal never proves removal. After logical `git worktree remove`, the worktree-root namespace parent and the nearest surviving Git-admin namespace parent are full-synced before any branch handling. Failure returns workspace_removed:null/uncertain, retains the prepared journal, performs no branch deletion, and writes no final receipt. A present root is pre-removal only when its root and Git-admin device/inode/ctime identities still exactly match the prepared operation. A same-path replacement is uncertain and the journal survives. Root-absent+unregistered reconciliation explicitly re-syncs those namespaces before trusting visible absence, durably writes removed phase before branch handling, persists a certified branch result before one operation-idempotent receipt, performs exact challenge/active-root/current-session cleanup, and writes finalized state. Legacy journals can finalize absent+unregistered state, but present state without physical identity remains uncertain. Signal disagreement, inaccessible signals, or malformed bound state preserves explicit uncertainty.
awa_finish_removal.recovery_rule: The shell immediately invokes local reconciliation if the finish child exits without valid JSON, and a later bound execution reconciles an existing journal before one-use challenge handling. Removal and reconciliation perform zero network calls. A visible namespace change after failed parent sync is not trusted in-process: recovery must explicitly re-adopt/re-sync it. Branch deletion uses explicit Git reference-fsync settings and then physically syncs the actual files backend namespaces (loose refs/reflogs/packed-refs and directories) or reftable list/table/common namespaces. If logical deletion occurs but that sync or the branch-journal write fails, branch truth remains uncertain, no receipt/finalized journal is minted, and recovery re-syncs exact backend state before classifying. Receipt failure leaves a removed-phase journal retryable; cleanup faults after certified removal are bounded warnings. Branch truth comes only from the validated durable journal; retained/deleted is never fabricated from an in-memory fallback. The current conversation index remains the exact terminal recovery anchor until complete removed/uncertain public JSON has been written and flushed; dialogue and envelopes may be cleaned first, and recovery validates the index with its bound journal without requiring the dialogue or removed root. Only then is that exact index generation CAS-deleted; output interruption or index deletion failure permits duplicate truthful recovery, while superseding generations remain untouched.
awa_finish_removal.storage: removal-<sha256-operation-id>.json under ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/awa/finish (dir 700, file 600), atomic replace with file and parent-directory fsync.
awa_finish_removal.note: NEW OPTIONAL top-level block and OPTIONAL clean_receipt operation_id, additive-within v1 (2026-07-11 second safety hardening); NO v2.

intent.rule: A deterministic high-signal recognizer runs before generic router normalization. It is recall-only: a match may create a Phase-1 preview/challenge but never authorizes removal. Negated, quoted, documentation, feature-request, hypothetical, code/example, and metalinguistic uses reject.

warning.rule: The approved static payload is immutable and byte-snapshot-tested; each of the five operator options (Commit, Retain, Mixed, Cancel, Close) is separated by a blank line so the Markdown-rendered modal shows each on its own line instead of reflowing them into one paragraph. Only escaped numbered rows after the final heading are dynamic; C0, DEL, all C1 controls, bidi controls, surrogates, and Markdown metacharacters never render raw. There is no row limit or truncation. Canonical shallow rows represent physical untracked/ignored trees containing only directories, so `None | No operator work will be deleted.` is emitted only when no visible file or directory-tree work would be deleted. The egress exception is scoped only to this exact template plus valid rows.

dialogue.exact_choice_rule: Commit, Retain, Mixed, and Cancel are case-insensitive standalone strings and may normalize reasonable leading/trailing whitespace to their canonical title-case values. Close remains only the exact literal `Close` with no surrounding whitespace. Attachments, extra words, booleans, yes, approval clicks, and model assertions are never terminal choices.
dialogue.close_rule: Only an envelope whose submitted text is exactly `Close` can activate the Close dispatcher path and invoke `clean --finish-current --authorization Close --conversation-id ... --expected-nonce ... --expected-generation ...`; case or trim variants return a deterministic non-destructive correction while leaving the pending dialogue live. The kernel independently requires exact hook-generation binding, atomically claims that generation before the shared-lock attempt, and under lock requires either the exact full-content challenge or its exact path-granularity structural proof. The latter may tolerate regular-file creation/removal/rename/mode/byte changes only below an unchanged displayed directory scope. Displayed-row insertion/removal/reorder/path/root-type/root-mode/root-link drift, directory/symlink descendant drift, structure drift outside such a scope, Git structure, operation, target, and membership drift refuse.
dialogue.cancel_rule: Cancel atomically marks the selected nonce+generation terminal before bounded dialogue/challenge/index/envelope projection cleanup and performs no repo, git, archive, worktree, or network mutation. Readers cannot resolve terminal projections; incomplete cleanup is reported as failure, never success.
dialogue.resolve_rule: Commit, Retain, and Mixed require explicit row selection and then a full fresh preview; Close is never inferred or automatically run. After irreversible Commit delivery or Retain publication, the exact nonce+generation dialogue is first persisted as action_complete_refresh_pending with closed action-kind/completion fields. In hook mode the action CLI creates or publishes no replacement challenge: the next beforeSubmitPrompt detects the latch before recognizing any choice or intent, reruns fresh reconnaissance, discards that triggering prompt with the immutable full warning, and leaves the latch until the hook's exact post-output publication transition. Therefore even exact Close on that trigger only publishes; a second exact Close is required for one envelope and one kernel invocation. Faults before output, after output, or before publication retain retryable completed-action truth and retries never repeat the completed action. Non-hook callers retain direct refresh compatibility. Mixed is complete once both dispositions complete even if refresh fails.
dialogue.public_projection_rule: Every dispatch success, refusal, error, uncertain result, cancellation, and Close correction is built by one closed typed projection after authorization handling. It copies no child stdout/stderr, arbitrary exception text, kernel message, local path, object id, hash, prompt, extra child field, or unvalidated branch reason. Known closed FinishUXError reason tokens remain actionable, and inventory/physical/fingerprint drift refusals add fixed plain-language recovery text directing the operator to start finish again and use only freshly displayed row numbers. Unknown or hostile exception text remains generic operation_failed. Only fixed messages and declared outcome/reason/branch vocabularies are public. Proven removal reports workspace_removed=true only from an exact machine projection whose closed branch result agrees with exit status, or from exact bound-journal reconciliation; no default branch result is fabricated. Proven refusal reports false. Any post-invocation ambiguity reports null with no branch claim and stops. Cancel reports no repository mutation.
dialogue.cli_parse_rule: Consumer and kernel argument parsing occurs inside a closed public boundary with long-option abbreviation disabled on the root parser and every generated subparser. Unknown options, every proper long-option prefix, malformed numeric values, missing required values, and extra positionals emit identical fixed JSON on stdout, empty stderr, and exit 2 without echoing parser text or supplied values. Only exact --help remains argparse help on stdout with exit 0.

public_projection.shell_machine_rule: The consumer sets the internal machine-mode environment value to 1 only for its clean --finish-current child. The shell emits exactly one closed JSON shape: removed+finish_removed+validated branch result, refused+workspace_preserved, or uncertain+removal_uncertain. It copies no kernel message or extra field and never substitutes a branch result. Missing, malformed, truncated, oversized, duplicate-field, type/enum-invalid, contradictory, or extra-field output is untrusted; exit 0/3 alone never proves removal. Untrusted output is reconciled only from the exact bound kernel journal; without that proof the public result is workspace_removed=null with no branch claim.

current_index.rule: Atomic 0600 index bound to canonical physical root, actual Desktop session/conversation identity, generation, nonce, and fingerprint. Production dispatch --current requires exactly one matching live non-terminal record; absent, duplicate, stale, cancelled/claimed, cross-root/session, or generation mismatch refuses. After a removal attempt, an exact index plus one validated journal with matching root/session/conversation/generation/nonce/fingerprint is also a terminal recovery anchor even when dialogue and root are absent; it can yield only truthful removed or uncertain output, never workspace-preserved, and is released by exact CAS only after that output flushes.

choice_envelope.rule: beforeSubmitPrompt writes one atomic 0600 one-use envelope for an exact Close, a case-insensitive Commit/Retain/Mixed/Cancel candidate, or a non-authorizing Close case/trim correction. The additive optional canonical_choice records the pure canonical decision while exact_text preserves submitted text. Dispatch re-derives and verifies that decision, consumes exactly one matching envelope, and rejects attachment presence, replay, ambiguity, drift, or reconstructed model answers.

hook.rule: The user-level hook performs only bounded local preview and blocks only after a complete warning is ready. Publication is hook-owned and post-output: each installed-hook invocation uses a private random invocation ticket bound to exact conversation/session/root/generation/nonce/warning digest; hook-published accepts only that emitted generation, and completed-action refresh becomes choice-accepting only after the exact warning was written and kernel publication succeeded. Tickets carry no authority and direct/library publication remains compatible. Because sessionStart is fire-and-forget, the first prompt CAS-binds its documented session/conversation/root identity or attaches its first real conversation to the same partial session; cross-session, cross-conversation, malformed, and ambiguous bindings fail open without a confirmable challenge. Hook failure is globally fail-open and deletes partial pending state; primary, absent, multi-root, Cloud, and background contexts mint no challenge. Cloud/background detection checks top-level and nested tool_input sources plus documented environment signals: empty and explicit false/0/no/off are Desktop-negative; every other non-empty broker/background handle is unsupported. Kernel refusal remains authoritative with the hook absent.

observation.storage: At most 100 metadata-only 0600 records under the 0700 finish-hook-observations state directory.
observation.rule: Records contain event/key presence, identity/root resolution outcomes, decision, and output digest only. They never contain raw prompt text, row paths, file contents, or authorization and have no authorization role.

publication_ticket.storage: At most 100 atomic 0600 records under the 0700 finish-hook-publications state directory; stale invocation tickets are bounded and carry no cleanup/removal authority.
publication_ticket.rule: The installed shell creates one private random invocation id and uses it for both the hook-output child and post-output publication child. The ticket exact-binds conversation/session/root/generation/nonce plus immutable warning digest. Missing, malformed, stale, cross-generation, or mismatched tickets cannot publish. No invocation environment value preserves the direct/library compatibility path; an invalid supplied value never falls back to it.

commit_delivery.network_boundary: Network is allowed only in Commit/Mixed delivery. Preview, authorization, Close/removal, branch disposition, Cancel, and Retain are zero-network.
commit_delivery.proof_rule: One unambiguous GitHub repository with merge commits enabled; one merge-commit PR whose headRefOid exactly equals the preserved head OID; that OID incorporated into the live default branch; complete checks; SUCCESS/NEUTRAL/SKIPPED pass; zero checks pass only after bounded repeated stable authoritative empty observations. Squash/rebase-only repositories are unsupported by this action and fail before delivery is claimed. Every pending/failure/error/cancelled/timed-out/stale/action-required/unknown or unavailable/malformed/ambiguous result fails honestly.

selected_snapshot.rule: The single kernel-owned canonical snapshot binds exact selected status bytes, index stages/modes/OIDs, file modes/content hashes, symlink targets, absence/deletion, and complete recursively selected directory descendants without following links. Directory-only trees are represented by one shallowest eligible untracked/ignored row after excluding root and tracked/index-derived ancestors; private sorted members and modes remain fingerprint-bound, Commit-ineligible, and Retain-eligible. Restore creates directories top-down, reapplies modes bottom-up, and proves exact topology and modes. Suppression requires exact whole-object equality; any error or malformed artifact keeps the row visible.

publication.rule: A new artifact is trusted when its hidden committed marker is a private regular file whose artifact id and SHA-256 exactly match the final restore_proven:true manifest bytes, or after a sole final artifact with a matching valid pending witness is safely recovered. The writer fully syncs hidden staging, restore-proves it, writes and syncs the true manifest while hidden, writes a pending marker, renames staging to final and syncs the Retain root, then independently writes and parent-syncs a matching committed marker while pending remains. Pending removal is optional post-commit cleanup only. Final+valid committed is trusted; sole final+valid pending is preserved and promoted; staging/rollback+pending stays hidden/untrusted; mismatches and multiple payload candidates are preserved and surfaced through bounded retain-list publication warnings, never auto-deleted. Kernel row suppression additionally requires the exact current source snapshot.
publication.legacy_rule: A markerless protected v1 artifact remains listable, restorable, and explicitly deletable as legacy_unlatched so existing data is never lost, but it cannot suppress a source row. Existing manifests remain readable. Pending/staging/publication-tombstone state is hidden and safely inspected only when its marker-v1 manifest and per-common-dir lock prove ownership; recovery never deletes a sole durable payload candidate.

protected_retain.storage: protected-retain/retain-<128-bit-random-id> plus hidden pending/committed publication markers under ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/awa; directories 0700, regular files/manifests/markers 0600
protected_retain.rule: Only explicitly selected rows are represented, except that selecting one synthetic operation row atomically includes its raw index/conflict state and every manifest-bound worktree dependency. Typed entries include regular files, directory-only trees with exact topology/modes, absent/deleted paths, symlinks, git status/index snapshots, rename/conflict/staged metadata, ignore intent, and explicitly confirmed secrets. An operation artifact additionally publishes exact admin bytes/topology/modes/hashes, logical refs, raw index and stages, and a local same-object-format object pack sufficient after later GC/ref removal. Secret dependencies require --allow-secrets; ignored operation dependencies require --allow-ignored-dependencies. Nothing untracked/ignored is silently included. Restore/proof builds an isolated standalone repository, verifies exact admin/ref/index/worktree/object/digest state, then proves the operation-specific abort/reset on a separate copy with hooks disabled and without continue, merge drivers, or rebase exec. Suppression requires the committed marker, intact payload, exact current operation manifest/digest, exact source snapshot, and abort-proven=true. Existing file-only v1 artifacts remain readable. Every visible class=ignored row—file, directory, or secret—is deterministically commit_eligible=false and retain_eligible=true; finish never uses git add -f. Commit and the Mixed commit partition reject any Retain-only row before dialogue claim, Git mutation, artifact creation, or delivery. Artifact creation and restore proof hold the same per-common-dir lock ABI as finish/clean/engine maintenance. Failure preserves the original worktree and every durable artifact candidate.
protected_retain.lifecycle: list and restore are explicit; manual delete requires the exact artifact id as confirmation and is path-contained. protected=true excludes automatic pruning, and normal uninstall preserves protected-retain.

finish_conversation.note: NEW OPTIONAL top-level block, additive-within v1 (2026-07-10, Root-Bound Worktree Finish Phase 2). It adds recall/UX only and cannot weaken or replace Phase-1 literal-Close authority.

active_root.emitted_by_role: sessionStart hook (worktree-session.sh) refreshes a per-root heartbeat when the session is in a linked worktree (Safe Workspace); the guard hot-path (worktree-guard.sh) ALSO refreshes it (THROTTLED) on any command run in a linked worktree, so an actively-used session cannot lapse to STALE at the raw TTL (and a session where sessionStart never fired still becomes protected on its first command). A long-lived owner MAY also refresh WITH its pid for strong liveness.

sessions_field.note: ADDITIVE-WITHIN-v1 (2026-07-10) OPTIONAL `sessions` object mapping a stable session key -> {session_id, pid, boot_id, branch, git_common_dir, first_seen, last_heartbeat, last_heartbeat_epoch}. The FROZEN top-level keys are UNCHANGED and continue to reflect the FRESHEST heartbeat across sessions, so disposition() and every existing reader are unaffected. heartbeat() updates BOTH the freshest top-level and the caller's per-session entry (preserving per-session first_seen). A legacy single-session record (no `sessions` map) is normalized into one entry on read/write.
sessions_field.session_key_rule: session_key = 's-'+sha256(session_id)[:20] when a session_id is present, else the single stable 'unattributed' bucket (so many pid-less hookless callers do not each inflate membership).
sessions_field.finish_session_waiver: The root-bound finish path uses a finish-ONLY gate (finish_session_gate), NOT disposition(). It exact-validates every session member's object/keyset, derived key/session identity, strict positive non-boolean pid (or null), target branch/common_dir, boot id, and parseable internally consistent timestamps. It may WAIVE ONLY the CONFIRMING session's OWN pid-less, TTL-fresh heartbeat. It BLOCKS on: any malformed member; a missing or mismatched confirming member; any OTHER session fresh-by-TTL or pid-alive; ANY live pid (even the confirming session's); or corrupt/unreadable evidence. Fail-safe = block. A completely absent record does not block (nothing claims the root; the challenge target-binding + fingerprint gates still protect). disposition() and ordinary `clean --path` semantics are UNCHANGED.
sessions_field.finish_session_residual: RESIDUAL — pid-less session collapse when DEV_SESSION_ID is unset (documented, inside the explicitly-unsupported one-writer-per-worktree boundary). With NO per-session id, all pid-less hookless callers collapse into the single stable 'unattributed' session_key (per session_key_rule), so finish_session_gate cannot DISTINGUISH two CONCURRENT PID-LESS sessions in the SAME worktree: the confirming session's waiver of 'its own' pid-less TTL-fresh heartbeat can waive what is actually a SECOND pid-less session's heartbeat, so the gate may WAIVE rather than BLOCK. Scope bound: a LIVE-PID session on the same boot STILL blocks regardless of session identity (the gate blocks on ANY live pid), so the residual is SPECIFICALLY two-or-more concurrent PID-LESS sessions colliding in 'unattributed' — never a running-process session. Mitigation: propagate a real per-session id so each lands in its own s-<hash> bucket (the Phase 2 conversational surface does this automatically; an operator/harness sets DEV_SESSION_ID per agent for the same separation today). See SECURITY.md 'Finish-session gate residual'.

current_session_identity.rule: sessionStart parses a unique documented payload identity and, only after successful heartbeat revalidation, CAS-writes this atomic 0600 root-bound record with exact linked root/branch/common-dir under the shared lock; when the event lacks conversation_id it writes an empty partial conversation rather than inventing an alias. The first beforeSubmitPrompt for that exact session/root may CAS-attach its real conversation_id; another session, conversation, target, malformed record, or ambiguous root refuses. A structurally valid prior-boot projection may be replaced after live target recheck; malformed evidence is preserved. Guard refresh uses payload identity when unique, otherwise a complete record; unknown identity mints no heartbeat. A later validation failure CAS-removes only a just-created exact binding, never a superseding record. Confirmed finish removal and journal reconciliation delete only the exact root/session/conversation/branch/common-dir/boot identity under the shared lock. A superseding record is preserved; failed finish preserves the record; cleanup uncertainty is surfaced.

active_root.canonical_disposition: A root's disposition is computed by ONE source of truth (awa_roots.disposition): active | stale | dead | untracked | absent. The clean gate AND sessionStart guidance both consult it — there is no second definition.
active_root.removal_rule: An ACTIVE root BLOCKS removal (clean refuses, reason_code active_root). A STALE heartbeat (TTL-expired, or an owning process proven gone on the SAME boot) ALLOWS removal. A DEAD root (recorded path no longer exists) gets sessionStart guidance to recover from archives. Ordinary destructive clean must acquire the shared per-common-dir lock, then RE-READS the canonical disposition IMMEDIATELY before `git worktree remove`: a root re-activated mid-clean REFUSES (reason_code reactivated_during_clean). Missing/failed/empty/non-regular/unusable/open-failed/busy lock setup refuses even under --force; healthy v1 bundle/force/branch behavior is unchanged.
active_root.identity_rule: Keyed by the CANONICAL (realpath) root path so the heartbeat writer and the clean gate agree regardless of a symlinked prefix (e.g. macOS /tmp -> /private/tmp). pid is recorded ONLY by a long-lived owner; an ephemeral hook OMITS pid and relies on the TTL, so a would-be-instantly-dead pid never reads as stale.
active_root.unknown_evidence_blocks: UNKNOWN evidence (an unreadable record, an unparseable heartbeat time) resolves to `active` (blocks removal) — never silently treated as safe.
active_root.fail_closed_rule: Every UNCERTAIN gate outcome fails CLOSED (refuse), never open: canonical disposition unavailable -> reason_code disposition_unavailable; kernel lib missing -> reason_code roots_lib_missing; re-activation during clean -> reason_code reactivated_during_clean; shared destructive-lock setup/acquisition unavailable -> reason_code clean_lock_busy.
active_root.operator_override: An operator `--force` (the explicit ack) overrides ONLY a FAIL-SAFE active (unknown evidence — a corrupt/unparseable record — NOT backed by a live pid) or an unavailable/lib-missing gate; a GENUINE fresh-heartbeat or live-pid active is NEVER force-removable. `awa_roots.py forget --root <path>` clears a stuck record (agent-invoked on the operator's behalf; touches only kernel state, never git/worktrees).
active_root.lease_status_note: The removal gate consults ONLY this active_root heartbeat. The .awa/lease.json status:"active" field is NOT a removal-blocking signal — do not assume editing a lease changes removability.
active_root.heartbeat_linearization_rule: Every existing-record read/validate/merge/write performed by heartbeat() and every finish session-membership/current-session write uses the shared per-common-dir advisory lock ABI. Existing absent/legacy/current evidence is strictly validated while locked; only valid evidence is merged, structurally valid prior-boot members are replaced/pruned after target recheck, malformed/mixed evidence remains untouched, and finish preview mints no challenge on malformed evidence. Dual timestamp writers derive ISO from one epoch sample; only a known one-second legacy skew is normalized under lock. The writer revalidates canonical top-level, linked git-dir/common-dir, and branch identity inside the lock, so delayed heartbeat/binding cannot recreate a removed root. The frozen ordinary disposition()/clean --path v1 classification remains unchanged.
active_root.no_os_lock: Active worktrees are NOT made undeletable by an OS lock or macOS immutable (uchg) flag — disposition is advisory kernel state only. The shared lock serializes heartbeat and root-bound-finish state transitions; it does not itself prevent an unrelated process from removing a worktree.
active_root.ttl_env: AWA_HEARTBEAT_TTL_SECONDS overrides the default TTL (43200s / 12h), but is CLAMPED: <=0 / non-integer is treated as 'use default' and a positive value is floored at 300s, so a stray env export can never DISABLE protection. AWA_HEARTBEAT_REFRESH_THROTTLE (default 180s) bounds the guard hot-path refresh cost.
active_root.k2_todo: DEFERRED (K2 observability, not a safety gap): dead-root records + roots/ grow unbounded — add a prune/TTL + size cap. The safety-relevant record escape (`forget` / --force) already ships.
active_root.note: Additive-within v1 (a new OPTIONAL top-level schema block, 2026-07-08; fail-closed hardening + hot-path-refresh + TTL-clamp + operator-override fields added 2026-07-08; OPTIONAL per-session `sessions` map + finish-only per-session waiver added 2026-07-10 for Root-Bound Worktree Finish Phase 1); NO v2.

manifest.emitted_by_role: The ONE unified recovery-artifact manifest shape emitted by BOTH the KERNEL bundler (dev-worktree.sh `clean --bundle` → awa_bundle_ignored) and the ENGINE writers (recovery.py create_bundle/create_patch/create_worktree_archive). stdlib-only, zero-network.
manifest.identity_rule: artifact_id is collision-resistant '<kind>-<128-bit hex>'. A legacy artifact predating this shape is normalized on read (deterministic 'legacy-<sha256(name)[:32]>' id, kind inferred from the manifest name, size/mtime from disk) and permission-repaired BEFORE policy evaluation — never silently trusted.
manifest.protected_rule: protected:true (whole-worktree archives + kernel Retain artifacts) are NEVER automatically removed by TTL or pressure, and SURVIVE uninstall.

deletion_journal.role: A TRANSIENT, crash-resumable on-disk tombstone journal (under recovery/.trash) written BEFORE any unlink and removed after the durable tombstone is recorded. An interrupted deletion is completed idempotently by reconcile (`_resume`). A failed archive unlink is an ERROR (the artifact stays restorable), never a reported success.

tombstone.role: A DURABLE prune record (state db `recovery_tombstones`, append-only, keyed by artifact_id) so a recovery row/receipt never implies an expired archive is still restorable. Also reconciles the `recovery_artifacts` row to status='pruned'.

policy.age_clock_rule: The age clock starts when the SOURCE work is DELETED (recorded once in state `recovery_source_deleted`), not when the archive is created; while the source still exists the artifact never ages. Ordinary artifacts expire at the 7-day TTL. A 1-GiB soft watermark prunes the OLDEST ordinary artifacts (oldest-first) after a 24-hour minimum age; young or protected artifacts may honestly leave storage above the watermark. Without a state db, ordinary artifacts fail SAFE (never TTL/pressure eligible).

recovery_retention.single_evaluator_rule: Artifact creation (prune-on-creation), the sessionStart hook, `daemon run-once`, and manual `recover prune --maintenance` ALL call ONE engine evaluator (retention.run_maintenance) and ONE crash-resumable deletion transaction. The hook contains NO retention logic and never directly unlinks a file.
recovery_retention.trigger_rule: The DETERMINISTIC primary trigger is prune-on-creation (every artifact write runs the bounded pass, so storage self-limits without a schedule). The sessionStart hook (kernel/hooks/awa-recovery-maintenance.sh, SEPARATE from worktree-session.sh) and `daemon run-once` are OPPORTUNISTIC secondary triggers: quiet on success, throttled to at most once/24h (state retention_last_run_epoch), non-blocking. Correctness never depends on the nondeterministic session schedule.
recovery_retention.lock_rule: Every maintenance pass runs under the single global state-root lock (locks/recovery-maintenance.lock), using the SAME advisory-flock ABI + private-lockfile perms as the per-common-dir finish/clean/Retain lock, so at most one pass runs machine-wide; an opportunistic trigger acquires NON-BLOCKING and simply skips when a pass is already running.
recovery_retention.containment_rule: Every deletion target must be a NON-symlink file resolving beneath the physical recovery root (symlink/path-escape targets are refused, including via a tampered resume journal). Bounded retry/backoff (max 3 attempts) on a transient unlink; any residual/failure is surfaced as an ERROR — destructive uncertainty PRESERVES the artifact.
recovery_retention.permissions_rule: recovery dir + .trash are 0700; ordinary archives/manifests/journals are 0600; a protected artifact's archive + manifest are 0400. Legacy pairs are permission-repaired before policy evaluation.
recovery_retention.no_finish_path_rule: Retention/pruning is STRICTLY SEPARATE from the finish authorization + removal path. The exact-`Close` authorization and worktree removal contain NO retention logic; retention runs only in the ENGINE, off the kernel safety path (kernel-first: worktree cleanup stays correct with the engine absent).
recovery_retention.visibility_rule: Failed maintenance, protected-storage growth, and watermark overage surface in the dashboard (environment.recovery, additive) and in a bounded sessionStart context warning, so automatic cleanup never fails silently.
recovery_retention.storage: Artifacts + manifests under ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/awa/recovery (dir 700), transient deletion journals under recovery/.trash, durable tombstones + source-deletion clock in the state db. Local disk. Zero-network on every path.
recovery_retention.note: Additive-within v1 (a new OPTIONAL top-level schema block, 2026-07-12, for Root-Bound Worktree Finish Phase 3 — Recovery retention lifecycle). Existing awa-contract v1 consumers stay valid; NO v2.
